verdict.rationale: Anrok documents refund handling through its own Transactions API. Full refunds are posted as negative transactions via createOrUpdate, and partial refunds use createNegation plus a new transaction version. Saved transactions are associated with the appropriate tax return, and void removes a transaction from a finalized return. Missing for 10: explicit documentation that negative amounts carry into the next filing period's liability after a return is filed, named credit-note support, reporting-level treatment of refunds, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, refunds and credit notes adjust tax correctly — negative amounts flow through liability, reporting, and the next filing without manual journal fixes

citations.quote: Use createOrUpdate endpoint to create a negative transaction representing the refund.
Use createNegation endpoint to negate the original transaction. Use createOrUpdate endpoint to create a new version of the partially refunded transaction.
this endpoint also saves the transaction in Anrok and associates it with the appropriate tax return
If a transaction needs to be removed from a tax return after it has been finalized, void can be used to remove the transaction from an Anrok tax return.
